figure.name: Bernie Sanders
figure.role: U.S. senator and democratic-socialist politician focused on health care, inequality, labor, taxation, and public goods.
figure.hook: Sanders = democratic socialism in modern U.S. electoral politics.
whyHere: Sanders belongs here because he brings the language argument into the present United States.
He matters because opponents often use socialism as an attack word, while Sanders uses democratic socialism for electoral politics, public goods, labor, health care, taxation, and inequality.
figure.cleanIdea: Modern democratic-socialist politics can argue for public goods and social rights through elections, not one-party rule.

ideas.title: Democratic Socialism
ideas.plainDefinition: Democratic socialism links socialist goals to democracy, civil rights, elections, and public accountability.
ideas.context: In the Sanders path, democratic socialism is framed through campaigns, public goods, labor, health care, and taxation.
ideas.whyMatters: Democratic socialism matters because it keeps modern U.S. usage separate from communist-party rule.

ideas.title: Public Goods
ideas.plainDefinition: Public goods are goods or services that serve public life and are hard to reduce to one private buyer.
ideas.context: In the Sanders path, health care, education, labor protections, and public investment become political claims about shared social life.
ideas.whyMatters: Public goods matter because social funding needs careful language: public provision, social democracy, democratic socialism, and socialism are related but not identical.

ideas.title: Public Spending
ideas.plainDefinition: Public spending is government spending on services, infrastructure, benefits, wages, defense, or public investment.
ideas.context: In the Sanders path, public spending is part of democratic debate over what people fund together.
ideas.whyMatters: Public spending matters because collective funding is real, but the page still has to name the specific policy and ownership structure.
